title: Mahli Beardman Eyes Australia ODI Debut Against England After Injury Comeback
author: Tariq Mureed

body:
**Australia's rising fast bowler Mahli Beardman is determined to make up for lost time as he targets an ODI debut against England, while keeping his long-term Test ambitions firmly in sight.**

At just 21, Mahli Beardman is already being talked about as one of Australia's most promising fast-bowling prospects. But after another frustrating injury setback, the Western Australian quick is in no hurry to get ahead of himself.

For now, his focus is simple: stay healthy, play competitive cricket and make the most of every opportunity that comes his way.

Beardman is preparing to represent Western Australia against England at the WACA on Saturday, November 7, in a one-day match that could provide an important opportunity to impress Australia's national selectors.

With Australia set to begin their ODI series against England at Perth's Optus Stadium on November 13, Beardman hopes he might get the chance to make his debut in front of his home crowd.

"The selection is well above my head, so if that opportunity arrives, I'll try and grab it with both hands," Beardman told reporters on Thursday.

"I feel like I'm ready to go out and play some good cricket again."

![](/images/news/wp/Airborne-Cricket-Star-in-Orange-and-Black-1024x683.jpg)

## A Promising Career Interrupted by Injury

Beardman's rapid rise has attracted plenty of attention, particularly because of his ability to generate serious pace and trouble established international batters.

One of his standout moments came during last season's Big Bash League finals, when he went head-to-head with Australian batting star Steve Smith and eventually won their individual battle.

His performances helped strengthen his reputation as a potential future international star.

Beardman has spent time around Australia's national squads over the past two years and made his international debut in a T20I against Pakistan earlier in 2026.

He made an immediate impression, dismissing Shadab Khan and Shaheen Shah Afridi in consecutive deliveries during the closing stages of the innings.

He finished with figures of 2 for 33 from four overs, offering a glimpse of what he could bring to Australia's pace attack.

However, the excitement was short-lived.

A recurrence of a stress fracture in his lower back forced him out of action and ended his season just as he was beginning to build momentum.

The setback also denied him further international opportunities and delayed his anticipated Sheffield Shield debut.

"The timing of it was pretty rough," Beardman admitted, reflecting on an injury that arrived when he felt his bowling was coming together.

Rather than rushing his recovery, the young quick spent around four to five months rebuilding his strength in the gym.

The experience has also taught him the importance of understanding his body and managing the physical demands of fast bowling.

## Test Cricket Remains the Ultimate Goal

With several of Australia's established Test fast bowlers approaching the later stages of their careers, Beardman's name has increasingly appeared in conversations about the country's next generation of pace talent.

But the youngster knows there is still a long road ahead.

Despite the growing expectations, he has yet to make his first-class debut, and there is currently no confirmed date for his first Sheffield Shield appearance.

For Beardman, the priority is proving he can remain fit and handle the workload before taking the next step.

Red-ball cricket remains an important part of his ambitions, but he is approaching that challenge carefully.

"It's just prioritising getting back, playing cricket first, proving my fitness and that my body can handle it," he explained.

Rather than setting a deadline for his Shield debut, Beardman wants to assess his progress after each match, ensuring he is recovering properly without experiencing soreness or recurring symptoms.

It is a cautious approach, but one that could prove important for a young fast bowler whose career has already been interrupted by injury.

## Raw Pace and Growing Confidence

Beardman has shown encouraging signs since returning to competitive cricket, even though his performances have been somewhat inconsistent.

During Australia A's recent tour against India A, he produced an impressive display of fast bowling, troubling the opposition's top order with his pace and movement.

Capable of regularly reaching speeds in the mid-140s kph, Beardman combines his natural speed with the ability to swing the new ball and deliver an aggressive bouncer.

And he believes he can still bowl faster.

"I think the goal is as high as I can go," Beardman said when asked about his pace.

"I don't think there's a number. I still feel like I've got a decent way to go."

While his attacking ability has already caught the eye, Beardman is also working on becoming a more complete fast bowler.

He has been developing the defensive side of his game, particularly for situations in limited-overs cricket when batters are attacking and bowlers need to adjust their plans quickly.

The young quick understands that raw pace alone will not guarantee success at the highest level.

Learning how to respond under pressure, control scoring opportunities and adapt to different match situations will be equally important.

## Learning From Dennis Lillee

Beardman's development has also benefited from the guidance of Australian fast-bowling legend Dennis Lillee, who has mentored him for several years.

That experience has provided the youngster with valuable insight into the demands of professional fast bowling as he works toward establishing himself at the highest level.

His immediate challenge, however, is against England.

Western Australia's upcoming one-day fixture at the WACA will give Beardman an early opportunity to test himself against international opposition ahead of Australia's ODI series.

The match is expected to attract a crowd of around 4,500 at the revamped WACA, creating an exciting atmosphere for the young local fast bowler.

Beardman also sees the contest as an opportunity to study England's top-order batters and potentially share useful information with Australia's national squad.

"I think it's just an awesome hit out," he said.

"It's a great chance to really get some insight into their top order and how they play."

## A Big Opportunity Ahead

For Beardman, the coming weeks could represent an important step in a career that has already generated considerable excitement.

A strong performance against England could strengthen his case for selection in Australia's ODI squad, particularly with the series opener taking place in Perth.

But whether an international opportunity arrives immediately or further down the road, Beardman appears determined not to rush the process.

After months spent recovering from injury, simply being back on the field is a significant achievement.

His Test ambitions remain alive, his pace continues to excite, and his potential is clear.

Now comes the challenge of turning that promise into consistent performances.

For one of Australia's most exciting young fast bowlers, the next chapter is about staying fit, building confidence and letting his cricket do the talking.

body:
**Pakistan have made four changes to their Test squad ahead of the two-match home series against Sri Lanka, handing maiden call-ups to three promising domestic performers.**

The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has brought in fast bowlers Ali Shabbir and Saqib Khan, along with batter Muhammad Tayyab Arif and experienced all-rounder Aamir Jamal.

The changes come just days before the opening Test in Rawalpindi on November 9, with Pakistan looking to strengthen their squad for the home series.

Meanwhile, Abdullah Fazal and Ali Usman have been released from the squad. The PCB has not explained the reasons behind their departures.

All four incoming players recently featured for the Patron's XI in a three-day warm-up match against Sri Lanka at Islamabad Club from November 4 to 6.

## Domestic performances open the door

Aamir Jamal returns to the Test setup after producing some impressive performances in domestic cricket.

The pace-bowling all-rounder, who has already represented Pakistan in nine Tests, three ODIs and six T20Is, starred in the President's Trophy Grade-I final with figures of 7 for 32 and a valuable 55 with the bat. His efforts helped Markhor IT Solutions lift the trophy.

Jamal also made an impact while captaining Lahore Whites in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold, taking three wickets and scoring 74 and 23 in the opening round.

For Muhammad Tayyab Arif, the selection marks an important step in his career.

The right-handed batter has been rewarded for a strong first-class season with Kingsmen Academy, where he scored 727 runs in seven matches at an impressive average of 66.09, including three centuries.

## Young fast bowlers get their chance

Ali Shabbir is another exciting addition to Pakistan's pace attack.

The 19-year-old has taken 22 wickets in eight first-class appearances and strengthened his case for selection by picking up three wickets against Sri Lanka in the recent practice match.

Saqib Khan has also earned his opportunity after a standout domestic campaign.

The fast bowler played a major role in Karachi Blues' 2025–26 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy triumph, finishing with 47 wickets in nine matches at an average of 20.60. His best figures were 7 for 34.

Both bowlers will now have the opportunity to work alongside experienced members of Pakistan's Test squad as they push for their international debuts.

## Pakistan's 16-member Test squad

Babar Azam (captain), Aamir Jamal, Ali Shabbir, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ghazi Ghori (wicketkeeper), Mohammad Suleman, Mohammad Taha, Muhammad Tayyab Arif, Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicketkeeper), Salman Ali Agha, Sameer Minhas, Saqib Khan and Saud Shakeel.

## Pakistan vs Sri Lanka Test series schedule

**First Test:** November 9–13, 2026 Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, Rawalpindi

**Second Test:** November 17–21, 2026 Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore

With three uncapped players joining the squad and several domestic performers pushing for opportunities, Pakistan have added fresh competition ahead of the Sri Lanka series.

The opening Test in Rawalpindi will offer an early indication of how the selectors plan to balance youth and experience in the playing XI.

body:
**Pakistan and Sri Lanka will be looking to put their recent struggles behind them when the two teams meet in a two-match Test series beginning November 9 in Rawalpindi. With both sides searching for consistency, the contest offers an opportunity to regain confidence and return to winning ways.**

Neither team has enjoyed much success in Test cricket recently. Pakistan are coming off a disappointing 3-0 series defeat in England, while Sri Lanka are still searching for their first Test victory of 2026.

Although the series may have limited influence on the race for the World Test Championship (WTC) final, there is plenty at stake for both teams.

Pakistan are hoping that changes to their squad and coaching setup will bring better results. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, arrive with a new Test captain and a batting lineup determined to turn promising performances into victories.

## Pakistan look to turn things around

Pakistan's recent Test performances have raised questions about the team's direction.

Their defeat in England exposed problems with the batting lineup, while an inconsistent bowling attack struggled to maintain pressure throughout matches.

The hosts have won just two of their nine Tests in the current WTC cycle, leaving them near the bottom of the standings.

Babar Azam has returned to the Test captaincy following Shan Masood's departure, while Mike Hesson and Shaun Tait have taken on key coaching responsibilities.

Pakistan have also made late changes to their squad, releasing Abdullah Fazal and Ali Usman while adding Aamir Jamal, Ali Shabbir, Saqib Khan and Muhammad Tayyab Arif.

Three of the newcomers are uncapped, giving Pakistan an opportunity to introduce fresh talent into a side looking for stability.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-8-2026-09_30_48-AM-1-1024x683.jpg)

## Pakistan's pace-heavy selection raises questions

One of the biggest talking points ahead of the series is Pakistan's decision to leave out specialist spinners Noman Ali and Sajid Khan.

With Arafat Minhas the main spin-bowling option, the hosts appear ready to place greater responsibility on their fast bowlers.

Mohammad Abbas brings experience, while Razaullah offers raw pace. The additions of Ali Shabbir and Saqib Khan provide further depth to the seam attack.

Aamir Jamal could also prove valuable with his ability to contribute with both bat and ball.

The squad suggests Pakistan may prefer surfaces that offer assistance to fast bowlers rather than the turning tracks seen in some recent home Tests.

However, that strategy carries risks.

A seam-friendly surface could also give Sri Lanka's fast bowlers an opportunity to exploit Pakistan's batting weaknesses.

## Sri Lanka determined to end difficult run

Sri Lanka have endured their own frustrating period in Test cricket, but recent performances have offered reasons for encouragement.

Their hard-fought draw against India highlighted the resilience of a batting lineup featuring Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva.

Kusal Mendis will captain Sri Lanka in Test cricket for the first time, taking over at an important stage for the team.

The visitors also have a bowling attack capable of adapting to different conditions.

Left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya has previously enjoyed success against Pakistan, while Asitha Fernando and Dilshan Madushanka provide pace options.

Sri Lanka will be hoping their experienced players can deliver when it matters most, particularly against a Pakistan side that has struggled for consistency.

## Key players to watch

### Babar Azam

Pakistan's captain will be under the spotlight as he looks to rediscover his best form in Test cricket.

Babar has struggled to convert starts into substantial scores in recent years, and Pakistan will need him to provide stability in a relatively inexperienced batting lineup.

His ability to build partnerships and lead from the front could be crucial to the hosts' chances.

### Razaullah

The young Pakistan fast bowler attracted attention during the England tour with his pace and aggressive approach.

His performance at Edgbaston showed his potential, but maintaining that standard across a full Test series will be the next challenge.

If conditions favour fast bowling, Razaullah could become an important weapon for Pakistan.

### Sonal Dinusha

Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha arrives in Pakistan following an impressive run of performances.

The 25-year-old has scored three centuries in his last four Test innings, including two hundreds against India in his previous appearance.

His unbeaten 133 in the second innings helped Sri Lanka secure a hard-fought draw.

Another strong series would further strengthen his growing reputation in international cricket.

Pakistan's squad selection suggests the hosts may favour a pitch offering assistance to fast bowlers rather than one that turns sharply.

However, if the surface remains flat during the opening days, building a substantial first-innings total could be essential.

Both teams will need to assess conditions carefully before settling on their final playing XIs.

The weather is expected to remain mostly dry, although rain could interrupt play later in the match.

Conditions for the second Test in Lahore will become clearer closer to the game.

Both teams have players capable of changing a match, but consistency has remained a major concern.

title: Australia Drop Marnus Labuschagne for New Zealand Test Series After Prolonged Batting Struggles

body:
**Marnus Labuschagne has lost his place in Australia's Test side once again, with selectors deciding to move on from the struggling No.3 ahead of the four-match home series against New Zealand.**

Australia have made a significant call ahead of their home summer, confirming that Marnus Labuschagne will not feature in the upcoming Test series against New Zealand, beginning December 9 in Perth.

The decision marks the second time in 17 months that the former world No.1 Test batter has been left out of Australia's plans, following an extended period of disappointing performances.

Selection chair George Bailey confirmed the decision on Sunday, bringing an end to growing speculation about Labuschagne's position in the batting order.

Rather than leaving the 32-year-old waiting for the squad announcement, selectors have opted to give him clarity ahead of another round of Sheffield Shield cricket.

## A Difficult Run That Australia Could No Longer Ignore

For several years, Labuschagne was one of the most dependable batters in world cricket. His patience, concentration and ability to occupy the crease made him a central figure in Australia's Test batting lineup.

But the runs have become increasingly difficult to find.

His last Test century came during the 2023 Ashes, and he has now gone 49 consecutive Test innings without reaching three figures.

Since returning to the side after being dropped for last year's Caribbean tour, Labuschagne has averaged just 23.66 across 10 Tests, managing only two half-centuries in 19 innings.

His recent tour of South Africa did little to improve his position.

After failing to reach 40 in either of the opening two Tests, Labuschagne endured a particularly disappointing finish in Cape Town, scoring a duck in the first innings and just four runs in the second.

Those performances added to the pressure on a batter who has struggled to rediscover the consistency that once made him almost impossible to leave out.

## From the World's Best to Fighting for His Place

Labuschagne's decline is particularly striking when compared with his remarkable rise earlier in his career.

Between November 2019 and December 2022, he struck 10 Test centuries in just 36 innings, establishing himself among the world's leading batters.

Alongside Steve Smith, he formed the backbone of an Australian middle order that regularly frustrated opposition bowling attacks.

His outstanding performances eventually carried him to the top of the ICC Test batting rankings.

At one stage, Labuschagne averaged an extraordinary 60.82 after his first 30 Tests.

That figure has since fallen to 42.64 after 68 appearances, reflecting how dramatically his fortunes have changed.

The challenge is no longer simply about scoring another century. It is about rebuilding the confidence and consistency that defined his best years.

![](/images/news/wp/Australian-Cricketer-Walking-Off-Field-2-1024x769.jpg)

## Bailey Leaves the Door Open for a Comeback

Despite the disappointment, Australia's selectors are not treating Labuschagne's omission as the end of his international career.

Bailey acknowledged that the right-hander remains capable of returning to the side, potentially for Australia's Test assignments in India and England next year.

The selection chair made it clear that Labuschagne's quality is not in question. What has been missing is the weight of runs expected from a specialist top-order batter.

There have been encouraging starts, including opportunities in Darwin and South Africa, but Labuschagne has repeatedly failed to turn them into substantial scores.

For now, he will return to domestic cricket and captain Queensland, where a sustained run of strong performances could put him back in contention.

Australia's message is straightforward: the opportunity to return remains, but runs will have to make the case.

## Who Takes Australia's No.3 Spot?

With Labuschagne out of the picture, attention now turns to how Australia will reshape their batting order for the New Zealand series.

Steve Smith is expected to return after missing the final Test against South Africa in Cape Town because of a neck injury.

His availability will be an important factor as selectors work through their options.

Bailey indicated that several players are well positioned for selection, but the final squad will not be settled until after the next round of Sheffield Shield matches, which begins Wednesday.

That gives Australia's leading domestic batters another opportunity to strengthen their claims before the selectors make their final decisions.

Whoever replaces Labuschagne will inherit a demanding role in a batting lineup looking for greater stability after the South Africa series.

![](/images/news/wp/Australian-Cricketers-Walking-the-Pitch-1-1-1024x683.jpg)

## A Defining Period for Labuschagne

For Labuschagne, the coming months could prove crucial.

At 32, he still has time to revive his Test career, but the competition for places means a return is far from guaranteed.

His reputation was built on long innings, relentless preparation and an appetite for runs. Those qualities have not disappeared, even if the results have fallen well below expectations.

A productive Sheffield Shield campaign would give selectors a reason to reconsider him, particularly with major overseas assignments approaching.

For Australia, however, the immediate priority is finding a reliable No.3 who can deliver consistently against New Zealand.

The selectors have made their decision. Now Labuschagne faces the challenge of proving that he still belongs at the highest level.

title: David Warner Backs Usman Khawaja’s Sandpapergate Claims, Questions Cricket Australia’s Investigation
author: News Desk
summary: David Warner backs Usman Khawaja's Sandpapergate claims and questions Cricket Australia's investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
body:
![](/images/news/wp/Australian-Cricketers-Celebrating-Together-2.jpg)

**David Warner has thrown his full support behind Usman Khawaja’s explosive account of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, claiming Cricket Australia’s investigation failed to uncover the full story.**

Nearly eight years after Australian cricket was rocked by the sandpaper scandal in South Africa, the controversy is back in the spotlight.

This time, former Australian opener David Warner has publicly backed Usman Khawaja, whose upcoming autobiography *Sabr* raises fresh questions about what happened behind the scenes and how Cricket Australia handled the fallout.

Warner, who was handed a 12-month suspension following the infamous Cape Town Test, has described Khawaja’s version of events as accurate and called for greater accountability from those responsible for the original investigation.

## Warner Breaks His Silence

Speaking in an Instagram video from Nepal, where he is competing in the Nepal Premier League, Warner addressed the controversy after details from Khawaja’s book began making headlines.

He made it clear that he stands firmly behind his former teammate.

"It's 100% accurate what you've said," Warner stated, thanking Khawaja for speaking publicly about events that have followed Australian cricket for almost a decade.

Warner also rejected suggestions that Khawaja was revisiting the scandal simply to promote his autobiography.

According to Warner, Khawaja had documented events as they unfolded, keeping a personal record of what happened during that turbulent period.

For Warner, the latest revelations are not about reopening old rivalries or targeting individual players. He believes they raise serious questions about whether the investigation established the full extent of what occurred.

![](/images/news/wp/IMG_5200.jpg)

## Khawaja Raises Fresh Questions About Sandpapergate

In his autobiography *Sabr*, scheduled for publication on Tuesday, November 10, Khawaja challenges several aspects of the accepted account of the 2018 scandal.

One of his most significant allegations is that sandpaper had been used to alter the condition of the ball during the preceding Test in Gqeberha, then known as Port Elizabeth, before the incident that was exposed in Cape Town.

He also suggests that knowledge of the ball-tampering plans extended beyond the three players who were eventually punished.

Khawaja maintains that he repeatedly encouraged the Australian team to accept collective responsibility rather than allowing a small group of players to carry the entire blame.

Perhaps most strikingly, he claims Cricket Australia never interviewed him during its investigation, despite his knowledge of the events.

Those allegations have renewed debate about whether the original inquiry was sufficiently thorough.

## Warner Calls the Investigation Flawed

Warner was particularly critical of the way Cricket Australia conducted its investigation following the Cape Town Test.

He questioned how investigators could reach comprehensive conclusions without speaking to Khawaja, who was part of the Australian squad and, according to Warner, had been sitting beside Cameron Bancroft.

Warner described the process as rushed and poorly handled.

He argued that the focus should now shift away from questioning Khawaja's motives and towards examining whether those responsible for the investigation carried out their duties properly.

The former opener wants greater transparency and accountability, insisting that the public deserves a clearer understanding of what happened.

His comments represent one of his strongest public interventions on the scandal since his suspension in 2018.

> A post shared by David Warner (@davidwarner31)

## The Scandal That Shook Australian Cricket

The controversy dates back to Australia's third Test against South Africa at Newlands, Cape Town, in March 2018.

Television cameras caught Cameron Bancroft attempting to alter the condition of the ball using sandpaper, triggering one of the biggest crises in Australian cricket history.

The fallout was immediate.

Then-captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner were each suspended from international and domestic cricket for 12 months, while Bancroft received a nine-month ban.

Warner was also handed a lifetime leadership ban, which was eventually overturned in 2024.

The scandal damaged the reputation of Australian cricket and left lasting consequences for the players involved.

Although all three eventually returned to professional cricket, questions about who knew what and when have continued to surface.

Khawaja's new account has brought those unresolved questions back into public discussion.

![](/images/news/wp/Australian-Cricketer-at-Press-Conference-1024x683.jpg)

## Cricket Australia Stands by Its Findings

Despite the renewed criticism, Cricket Australia has defended the integrity of its original investigation.

In a statement issued over the weekend, the governing body acknowledged the continuing speculation surrounding the 2018 incident but maintained that all relevant information submitted to it had been appropriately considered.

Cricket Australia said it remained satisfied with the findings of its integrity process.

The organisation also stressed that anyone with additional information could still bring it forward for consideration.

Its position leaves a clear disagreement between the governing body and the accounts now being presented by Khawaja and Warner.

While Warner believes the investigation was incomplete, Cricket Australia has given no indication that it intends to overturn its original conclusions.

## Warner Reveals the Personal Toll

Beyond the questions surrounding the investigation, Warner also spoke about the impact the scandal has had on his family.

He explained that he had taken several days to respond to Khawaja's revelations because he first wanted to discuss the matter with his children.

The former Australian opener said explaining the images and events from 2018 to his daughters had been particularly difficult.

He used the conversation to emphasise the importance of telling the truth, even when doing so is uncomfortable.

Warner also acknowledged the difficult years experienced by the families of Smith and Bancroft.

His remarks offered a personal perspective on a controversy that has often been discussed primarily through suspensions, investigations and sporting consequences.

![](/images/news/wp/Australian-Cricketers-Celebrating-Together-1-1-1024x683.jpg)

## Questions Remain for Australia's 2018 Players

Although the Cricket Australia executives involved in the original investigation have since left their positions, several members of the 2018 Australian squad remain active in international cricket.

Mitchell Starc is expected to face questions from the media at a commercial event on Tuesday, while Mitchell Marsh is scheduled to speak on Thursday ahead of Australia's ODI series against England.

Their appearances could provide further opportunities for journalists to seek clarification about the claims.

The controversy has also brought renewed attention to comments made by Bancroft in 2021, when he suggested that knowledge of the ball-tampering activities among Australia's bowlers was "self explanatory".

That interview prompted a response from the bowlers involved, who disputed suggestions that they had known about the use of a foreign substance on the ball.

Khawaja's autobiography also discusses a conversation with Todd Greenberg, now Cricket Australia's chief executive, who was leading the Australian Cricketers' Association at the time.

## A Scandal That Refuses to Fade

Eight years on, Sandpapergate remains one of the most controversial episodes in Australian cricket.

The punishments handed to Warner, Smith and Bancroft are well documented, but Khawaja's allegations have reopened questions about the wider team's knowledge and the scope of Cricket Australia's investigation.

Warner's public endorsement adds weight to Khawaja's account, although the new allegations remain disputed and have not been independently established.

For now, Cricket Australia continues to stand by its findings, while Warner and Khawaja are pushing for a more complete examination of the events.

With *Sabr* set for release and more members of the 2018 squad expected to face the media, the debate surrounding Australian cricket's most infamous ball-tampering scandal appears far from over.

title: Cricket Australia Rules Out Fresh Sandpapergate Investigation Despite Khawaja's Claims
author: News Desk
summary: Cricket Australia rules out a new Sandpapergate investigation as Usman Khawaja's claims and David Warner's support reignite debate.
body:
![](/images/news/wp/Outdoor-Media-Briefing-with-Microphone-Cluster-1024x683.jpg)

**Cricket Australia has rejected calls to reopen its investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, even as fresh allegations from Usman Khawaja and support from David Warner raise new questions about what really happened in South Africa.**

The Sandpapergate controversy is once again dominating Australian cricket, but Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has made it clear that the governing body has no plans to revisit the original investigation.

Speaking to SEN on Tuesday, November 10, Greenberg defended the decision to move forward rather than reopen a case that led to lengthy suspensions for Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.

His comments follow the release of Khawaja's autobiography *Sabr*, in which the veteran Australian batter challenges the accepted account of the scandal and argues that responsibility extended beyond the three players who were punished.

## Todd Greenberg Says It's Time to Move Forward

Greenberg believes another investigation would achieve little, particularly given the conflicting accounts that have emerged over the past eight years.

"There's absolutely no benefit going back," Greenberg told SEN, explaining that Cricket Australia's board supports leaving the original investigation closed.

He acknowledged that different players have offered different versions of the same events, making it difficult to reach a conclusion that everyone would accept.

Rather than revisit decisions made in 2018, Greenberg wants Australian cricket to focus on the future.

However, his position is unlikely to satisfy those who believe important questions remain unanswered.

## Khawaja Says the Entire Team Shared Responsibility

Khawaja's autobiography has brought fresh attention to the events surrounding Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa.

The experienced opener argues that the scandal should never have been treated as the responsibility of just three individuals.

Speaking to Nine ahead of his book's release, Khawaja stressed that the entire Australian setup needed to acknowledge its role.

"It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," Khawaja said.

He also expressed frustration that, nearly eight years after the incident, the full story had still not emerged.

Khawaja maintains that he never wanted to be the person publicly revisiting the controversy. However, he felt compelled to share his account after waiting years for what he considers the complete truth to come out.

His book also raises questions about whether sandpaper was used during the preceding Test in Port Elizabeth, before the incident that was exposed in Cape Town.

Those allegations remain disputed.

![](/images/news/wp/IMG_5200-2.jpg)

## David Warner Backs Khawaja's Account

Former Australian opener David Warner has publicly supported Khawaja's version of events, adding another layer to the growing controversy.

Warner, who received a 12-month suspension following the Cape Town scandal, has criticised Cricket Australia's original investigation and questioned whether it was sufficiently thorough.

He has described Khawaja's account as accurate and called for greater transparency over the handling of the case.

Warner's intervention is significant because he was one of the central figures punished in 2018.

His support has also intensified debate over whether the investigation fully examined the involvement and knowledge of others within the Australian camp.

Despite his criticism, Warner has framed his comments around accountability rather than a desire to target former teammates.

> A post shared by David Warner (@davidwarner31)

## Australia's Bowlers Have Previously Denied Knowing About Sandpaper

One of the biggest points of disagreement concerns what Australia's bowlers knew about the ball-tampering plans.

In 2021, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon issued a joint statement denying knowledge that a foreign substance had been brought onto the field to alter the ball.

Their position remains an important part of the debate, particularly as Khawaja's account suggests a broader level of responsibility within the team.

Greenberg acknowledged that some details in Khawaja's book conflict with accounts previously provided by other players.

He urged caution when interpreting the allegations, arguing that Khawaja's actual words should be considered rather than relying solely on headlines or public reactions.

The Cricket Australia chief also suggested that future autobiographies from other members of the squad could present further differing accounts of the same controversy.

## Michael Clarke Wants the Full Truth

Former Australian captain Michael Clarke has taken a different position from Greenberg, arguing that the unresolved questions are precisely why the controversy continues to follow Australian cricket.

Speaking on 2DayFM Breakfast, Clarke said fans had never been given the clarity needed to put the scandal behind them.

He believes the opportunity to establish the full truth was missed in 2018 and again in 2021, when Bancroft's comments reignited debate about who knew of the ball-tampering plans.

Clarke wants answers to two particularly important questions.

First, how many members of the Australian team knew that sandpaper was being used?

Second, did similar ball-tampering take place during the previous Test in Port Elizabeth?

For Clarke, resolving those questions is essential if Australian cricket wants to move beyond the controversy.

He argued that the continuing uncertainty has damaged public trust and left supporters unsure which version of events to believe.

## What Happened During the 2018 Sandpapergate Scandal?

The controversy began during Australia's third Test against South Africa at Newlands in Cape Town in March 2018.

Television cameras captured Cameron Bancroft attempting to alter the condition of the ball using yellow sandpaper.

The incident triggered widespread criticism and a major investigation by Cricket Australia.

Then-captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner received 12-month suspensions, while Bancroft was banned for nine months.

Warner was also handed a lifetime leadership ban, which was eventually overturned in 2024.

The punishments became one of the defining moments in modern Australian cricket, with the scandal affecting careers, reputations and public confidence in the national team.

Although the three players eventually returned to professional cricket, questions about the wider team's involvement have never entirely disappeared.

## Current Australian Players Could Face More Questions

Greenberg expects the controversy to remain a topic of discussion as members of Australia's current squad face the media.

He indicated that captain Pat Cummins and other players would likely be asked about the allegations in the coming days and weeks.

That could place renewed attention on players who were part of the 2018 tour and have previously addressed the scandal.

For Cricket Australia, the challenge is now managing a growing public debate while maintaining confidence in the findings of its original investigation.

For Khawaja, Warner and those calling for greater scrutiny, the issue remains whether the complete account of what happened has ever been established.

## Sandpapergate Remains an Unfinished Story

Eight years after the Cape Town incident, Australian cricket is still divided over how much of the truth has been revealed.

Khawaja believes responsibility extended beyond the punished trio. Warner has backed his account. Clarke wants the unanswered questions examined.

Cricket Australia, however, remains satisfied with its original findings and has ruled out reopening the investigation.

The governing body's decision may settle its official position, but it is unlikely to end the public debate.

With conflicting accounts still emerging and current players expected to face further questions, Sandpapergate continues to cast a shadow over Australian cricket.

For now, the central issue remains unresolved: whether the original investigation established the full extent of what happened in South Africa.

title: Pakistan Dominate Sri Lanka as Saud Shakeel's 93 Sets Up Strong Day Two in Rawalpindi

summary: Pakistan dominate Sri Lanka on Day 2 in Rawalpindi as Saud Shakeel scores 93. Sri Lanka reach 114/3 at stumps, trailing by 320 runs.
body:
![](/images/news/wp/Pakistani-Cricket-Teammates-on-the-Field-1024x683.jpg)

**RAWALPINDI:** Pakistan tightened their grip on the first Test against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, piling up 434 for nine declared before their fast bowlers struck three times to leave the visitors facing an uphill battle at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.

Sri Lanka reached 114 for three when poor light brought an early end to the second day's play, still trailing by 320 runs. Kamindu Mendis was unbeaten on 40 alongside captain Dhananjaya de Silva, who had made 22.

It was another productive day for Pakistan, with Saud Shakeel leading the batting effort and debutant Saqib Khan making an immediate impression with the ball.

## Saud Shakeel falls short of century as Pakistan pile on the runs

Pakistan resumed on 281 for five and showed little urgency to declare, choosing instead to build a total that would put Sri Lanka under sustained pressure.

Shakeel, who had reached his half-century on the opening day, continued to anchor the innings. He found valuable support from debutant Ghazi Ghori, with the pair adding 96 runs for the sixth wicket.

For much of the morning, Shakeel looked on course for a well-deserved century. But his innings ended on 93 from 199 deliveries when Asitha Fernando had him caught behind, leaving the left-hander just seven runs short of three figures.

Ghori also played his part, contributing 48 before departing.

Pakistan's lower order kept the scoreboard moving, with debutant Arafat Minhas producing one of the day's most entertaining knocks. The youngster struck 52 from 72 balls, hitting nine fours and a six to maintain the pressure on Sri Lanka's bowlers.

Dilshan Madushanka eventually removed Minhas, while Razaullah chipped in with a quick 10 before Pakistan declared at 434 for nine in the 107th over.

![](/images/news/wp/Pakistani-Cricketer-Under-Stadium-Lights-1024x683.jpg)

## Five half-centuries underline Pakistan's batting depth

Pakistan's first innings was built around contributions from across the batting order rather than one dominant individual performance.

Five batters passed fifty, including three players making their Test debuts.

Tayyab Arif scored 57, Mohammad Taha contributed 51 and Arafat Minhas added 52. Captain Babar Azam also reached his half-century, while Shakeel's 93 remained the highest score of the innings.

The contributions from Pakistan's newcomers were particularly encouraging, giving the hosts a substantial total and demonstrating the depth of their batting lineup.

For Sri Lanka, Fernando and Madushanka claimed three wickets apiece, but the visitors struggled to prevent Pakistan from building partnerships throughout the innings.

## Saqib Khan strikes twice as Sri Lanka stumble

Sri Lanka's reply began badly, with Mohammad Abbas dismissing opener Pasindu Sooriyabandara without scoring.

The early breakthrough gave Pakistan the opening they wanted, and debutant Saqib Khan soon added to Sri Lanka's problems.

Saqib removed experienced batter Dinesh Chandimal for just one, putting the visitors under immediate pressure.

Lahiru Udara attempted to steady the innings with a determined 42, but his resistance ended when Saqib struck for the second time, with Ghazi Ghori completing the catch behind the stumps.

The two wickets capped an impressive opening spell for the debutant and left Sri Lanka searching for a way back into the contest.

![](/images/news/wp/Pakistani-Bowlers-Triumphant-Celebration-1-2-1024x683.jpg)

## Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva offer resistance

With three wickets down, Sri Lanka needed a partnership to prevent the situation from deteriorating further.

Kamindu Mendis and captain Dhananjaya de Silva responded with an unbeaten 49-run stand

title: ICC Meeting in Bali Could Shape the Future of World Cricket as Financial Pressure Mounts
author: Tariq Mureed
tags: ICC Meeting 2026, BCCI, Cricket Finance, World Cricket, ICC, International Cricket, ICC Revenue Distribution
summary: ICC meeting could reshape cricket's future as global boards confront falling broadcast revenue and financial inequality.
body:
![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-11-2026-09_50_54-AM.jpg)

**Cricket is facing a financial crossroads, and the decisions made at this week's International Cricket Council (ICC) meeting in Bali could have lasting consequences for the global game.**

The ICC is preparing to discuss a major strategic review as concerns grow over declining broadcast revenues, unequal distribution of wealth and the future of international cricket.

At the heart of the discussions is a report commissioned by the ICC and prepared by global consulting firm McKinsey & Company. The review examines the financial and structural challenges facing cricket and the changes that may be needed to protect its future.

For years, the sport has relied heavily on television and digital broadcasting agreements to fund international competitions and support national cricket boards. That model is now facing growing pressure.

And this time, even some of cricket's wealthiest governing bodies have reasons to be concerned.

## Cricket's Heavy Dependence on Indian Broadcast Revenue

India remains the financial powerhouse of world cricket.

According to figures cited in the original report, Indian broadcasting rights account for approximately 75% of the ICC's media rights value, highlighting just how dependent the international game has become on one market.

JioHotstar's broadcasting agreements include approximately $3 billion for Indian Premier League (IPL) rights covering 2024 to 2027, alongside a further $720 million for Indian international and domestic cricket rights from 2023 to 2028.

These agreements have helped drive cricket's commercial growth, but concerns are emerging over whether future deals can command similar prices.

If broadcasting companies reduce their spending during the next rights cycle, the consequences could extend far beyond India.

The ICC distributes a significant portion of its revenue among member nations, many of which depend on those payments to operate their cricket programmes.

A smaller broadcasting deal could therefore mean less money for cricket boards around the world.

## ICC Revenue Distribution Under Growing Scrutiny

The current ICC financial model has long been a subject of debate.

Under the 2024–2027 revenue distribution arrangement, India receives approximately 38.5% of the ICC's income, reflecting its enormous contribution to the sport's commercial value.

Bangladesh receives around 4.46%, while the 99 Associate members collectively share approximately 11.19%.

The differences are substantial.

For financially stronger cricket boards, a reduction in ICC distributions could mean difficult budget decisions. For smaller nations, the impact could be much more serious.

Development programmes, domestic competitions, coaching structures and international tours all require funding.

If that funding declines, the gap between cricket's established powers and emerging nations could grow even wider.

According to a previously reported internal document from Cricket Netherlands, the ICC had warned of a possible 30% reduction in revenue in 2028 following the renewal of media rights agreements.

That figure represents a warning rather than a confirmed outcome, but it illustrates the scale of the financial uncertainty.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-11-2026-09_50_38-AM.webp)

## Even England and Australia Are Feeling the Pressure

Financial difficulties are no longer limited to cricket's smaller nations.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is reportedly forecasting losses of up to £50 million next year, despite the commercial appeal of hosting an Ashes series.

One contributing factor is the ICC's decision to retain a portion of broadcasting distributions to help cushion the potential impact of future revenue declines.

The situation raises an uncomfortable question for international cricket.

If a major cricket board struggles to generate a surplus during an Ashes summer, what does that mean for countries whose bilateral series attract significantly smaller audiences and broadcasting deals?

For many national boards, hosting international cricket is already expensive.

Touring arrangements, stadium operations, player payments, security and broadcasting production all add to the cost.

Without sufficient commercial income, even competitive international series can become financial liabilities.

## Why Bilateral Cricket Faces an Uncertain Future

Outside the sport's biggest markets, bilateral international cricket has become increasingly difficult to sustain financially.

The original analysis estimates that bilateral cricket involving nations outside India, England and Australia generates less than 4% of the sport's combined global revenue.

That creates a serious imbalance between the cost of staging matches and the income they generate.

Bangladesh offers an example of the challenge.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board reportedly struggled to secure broadcasting arrangements for its home Test series against West Indies after plans to package its 2026–27 international rights together were disrupted by uncertainty surrounding an India tour.

Reports also suggest that Bangladesh recorded financial losses in seven of nine home international series between 2022 and 2025, with tours involving India and England providing the profitable exceptions.

For boards in similar positions, hosting India can make a major difference to annual revenue.

But that dependence also leaves them vulnerable.

If Indian broadcasting rights lose value, the financial benefits associated with those tours may also come under pressure.

The result could be fewer profitable international fixtures and greater difficulty maintaining regular bilateral cricket.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-11-2026-09_53_47-AM.jpg)

## A Crowded Calendar Makes Reform More Difficult

Money is only one part of cricket's problem.

The international calendar has become increasingly congested, with Test cricket, bilateral white-ball series, ICC tournaments and domestic franchise leagues competing for space.

Players face demanding schedules, while national boards must balance international commitments against the commercial opportunities offered by franchise competitions.

The challenge is not simply finding more matches to play.

It is creating a schedule that makes financial sense while protecting the different formats of the game.

Proposals for additional international competitions, including a World Club Championship, have already faced obstacles.

Reports also indicate that the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), ECB and Cricket Australia have expressed reservations about expanding triangular and quadrangular series because of existing scheduling pressures.

Any meaningful restructuring would require agreement among cricket's most influential governing bodies.

That may prove difficult when different boards have different financial priorities.

## Can the ICC Bring Cricket's Biggest Boards Together?

The ICC's governance structure adds another layer of complexity.

Unlike a centralised sports league, international cricket operates through national governing bodies that retain considerable influence over their own fixtures and commercial arrangements.

That means reforms designed to benefit the wider game may not always align with the immediate financial interests of individual boards.

The World Cricketers' Association has previously raised concerns about the sport's fragmented structure and the lack of a coordinated global calendar.

Paul Marsh, who helped prepare a WCA report on cricket's future, has argued that the sport is failing to make full use of its international growth potential.

His concerns centre on governance, scheduling and the competing interests of national cricket boards.

The ICC's challenge is to find a model that allows the game's biggest commercial markets to prosper while providing smaller nations with enough financial security to develop.

That could involve changes to revenue distribution, more coordinated scheduling and new ways of generating income beyond traditional broadcasting contracts.

However, the strategic review's recommendations have not yet been formally adopted, and there is no guarantee that the meeting will produce immediate reforms.

## Why the Bali Meeting Matters for Cricket's Future

The ICC's meeting in Bali arrives at a particularly important moment.

Cricket has enjoyed significant commercial growth through the IPL, international tournaments and the expansion of franchise leagues.

Yet that success has not translated into equal financial stability across the sport.

Many cricket boards remain heavily dependent on ICC distributions and occasional high-value bilateral tours.

At the same time, concerns about future broadcasting deals are forcing administrators to reconsider whether the current financial structure can remain sustainable.

The McKinsey review gives the ICC an opportunity to examine those weaknesses and consider a more coordinated approach.

The bigger question is whether cricket's most powerful stakeholders can agree on changes that serve the long-term interests of the entire sport.

**Cricket does not lack global appeal. What it needs is a financial and competitive structure capable of supporting that appeal across more nations.**

The decisions taken in Bali may not solve every problem immediately, but they could reveal whether the ICC and its members are prepared to confront the challenges that have been building for years.

title: De Silva and Mendis Centuries Put Sri Lanka in Command Against Pakistan
author: Azmat Nawaz
summary: De Silva hits 167* and Kusal Mendis scores 117* as Sri Lanka reach 404-4 on Day 3 of the first Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi.
body:
**RAWALPINDI, November 11:** Sri Lanka turned the first Test against Pakistan on its head on Wednesday as Dhananjaya de Silva and newly appointed captain Kusal Mendis struck unbeaten centuries to put the visitors firmly back in contention on the third day in Rawalpindi.

After struggling at 114-3 overnight, Sri Lanka finished the day on 404-4, just 30 runs behind Pakistan's first-innings total of 434-9 declared.

De Silva led the recovery with an unbeaten 167, while Mendis produced a commanding 117 not out. Together, they added 249 runs for the fifth wicket, frustrating Pakistan's bowlers and shifting the momentum towards the visitors.

## Mendis Makes History in First Test as Captain

For Kusal Mendis, the innings carried extra significance.

Playing his first Test since taking over the captaincy from De Silva, the 31-year-old became the first Sri Lankan batter to score a century on his Test captaincy debut.

Mendis looked confident throughout his innings, mixing controlled strokeplay with attacking shots. His unbeaten 117 featured 10 fours and four sixes as he repeatedly punished loose deliveries.

He reached his 11th Test century in memorable fashion, guiding a delivery from Razaullah over the wicketkeeper for four.

At the other end, De Silva provided the stability Sri Lanka needed, patiently building his innings before accelerating as Pakistan's bowlers began to tire.

The former captain brought up his 14th Test hundred with a boundary off spinner Arafat Minhas. It was his fourth century against Pakistan and his second at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.

His unbeaten 167 came from 241 deliveries and included 20 boundaries.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-11-2026-11_36_39-AM-1-1024x683.jpg)

## A Record Partnership That Changed the Match

The two batters did more than rescue Sri Lanka from a difficult position. Their unbeaten 249-run stand also established a new record for the highest fifth-wicket partnership by Sri Lanka against Pakistan in Test cricket.

They surpassed the previous mark of 207, set by Thilan Samaraweera and Tillakaratne Dilshan in Lahore in 2009.

Pakistan had an opportunity to prevent the partnership from developing when Saud Shakeel dropped De Silva on 38 off Razaullah's bowling.

The missed chance proved costly.

De Silva settled into his innings, and once Mendis joined him, Pakistan struggled to create further opportunities.

The pair combined patience with aggression, rotating the strike comfortably and taking advantage whenever the bowlers missed their lengths.

By the time poor light brought an early end to proceedings, Sri Lanka had piled on 290 runs during the day without losing another wicket after Kamindu Mendis's dismissal.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-11-2026-11_36_47-AM-1024x683.jpg)

## Kamindu Sets the Stage for Sri Lanka's Recovery

Sri Lanka's fightback had begun earlier through De Silva and Kamindu Mendis, who added 90 runs for the fourth wicket.

Kamindu played a patient innings of 58 from 131 balls, striking eight boundaries before Mohammad Abbas finally broke the partnership.

The left-hander edged a delivery through to wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori, giving Pakistan a much-needed breakthrough.

But any hopes of quickly running through Sri Lanka's middle order disappeared as Kusal Mendis joined De Silva and took control.

Pakistan's bowlers were unable to build sustained pressure despite their promising start to the innings.

Abbas finished the day with figures of 2-64, while debutant Saqib Khan had taken 2-105.

## Pakistan's Strong Start Fades

Pakistan had appeared to be in a comfortable position after declaring their first innings at 434-9 on Tuesday.

Saud Shakeel top-scored with 93, narrowly missing out on a century, while debutants Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha and Arafat Minhas all contributed half-centuries.

The hosts then made early inroads with the ball, reducing Sri Lanka to 114-3 by the close of the second day.

At that stage, the visitors were still 320 runs behind and facing a difficult task to stay competitive.

Three sessions later, the picture looked completely different.

Sri Lanka's middle order had wiped out almost the entire deficit, leaving Pakistan searching for answers heading into the fourth day.

## An Intriguing Fourth Day Awaits

![](/images/news/wp/Pakistani-Cricket-Team-Celebration-1-1024x683.jpg)

With De Silva and Kusal Mendis both unbeaten and Sri Lanka trailing by only 30 runs, the visitors have an opportunity to build a substantial first-innings lead.

Pakistan, meanwhile, will need early wickets on Thursday to prevent the match from slipping further away.

What began as a promising Test for the hosts has developed into a fascinating contest, with Sri Lanka's remarkable recovery keeping both teams firmly in the battle.

The two sides will meet again in Rawalpindi for the second Test beginning November 17. The match was originally scheduled for Lahore but was relocated because of worsening smog conditions.

body:
**Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings have completed a major player swap ahead of IPL 2027, with Hardik Pandya heading to Punjab and Arshdeep Singh moving to Mumbai.**

Mumbai Indians (MI) and Punjab Kings (PBKS) have finalized one of the biggest trades ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League season, exchanging two of India's leading international cricketers.

Hardik Pandya, who captained Mumbai Indians for the past three seasons, will join Punjab Kings for INR 18 crore, an increase from his previous salary of INR 16.35 crore. Meanwhile, left-arm fast bowler Arshdeep Singh will move to Mumbai Indians at his existing contract value of INR 18 crore.

The deal marks a significant change for both franchises as they reshape their squads for the upcoming season.

## Mumbai Indians Prepare for Life Without Hardik

Hardik's departure brings an end to his second spell with Mumbai Indians, a franchise where he established himself as one of the IPL's most successful allrounders.

He began his IPL career with Mumbai in 2015 and played a key role in four of their championship-winning campaigns.

In 2022, Hardik joined Gujarat Titans as captain and immediately made an impact, leading the newly formed franchise to the IPL title in its debut season. He guided Gujarat to another final in 2023 before returning to Mumbai Indians as captain in 2024.

His return, however, did not produce the results Mumbai had hoped for.

The five-time champions finished at the bottom of the table in 2024, recovered to reach the playoffs in 2025, and slipped to ninth place in 2026.

Across 39 matches under Hardik's leadership, Mumbai recorded 15 victories and 24 defeats.

His departure now leaves the franchise searching for a new captain ahead of IPL 2027.

> A post shared by Mumbai Indians (@mumbaiindians)

## Arshdeep Singh Set to Partner Jasprit Bumrah

While Mumbai lose an experienced allrounder, they gain one of India's most established left-arm fast bowlers.

Arshdeep Singh arrives after spending eight seasons with Punjab Kings, the franchise where he made his IPL debut in 2019.

The 27-year-old claimed 111 wickets in 96 appearances for Punjab, becoming the franchise's leading wicket-taker in IPL history.

His arrival could give Mumbai Indians one of the competition's most dangerous pace combinations alongside Jasprit Bumrah.

With Bumrah's precision and Arshdeep's left-arm variation, Mumbai will have two experienced Indian fast bowlers capable of making an impact during the powerplay and at the death.

Mumbai Indians co-owner Akash Ambani welcomed Arshdeep's arrival, highlighting the experience, skill and competitive spirit he brings to the bowling attack.

![](/images/news/wp/Indian-Cricketers-Training-Under-Stadium-Lights-1024x683.jpg)

## A Fresh Start for Hardik at Punjab Kings

For Hardik, the move to Punjab Kings offers another opportunity to establish himself at a new franchise.

Punjab will become his third IPL team after Mumbai Indians and Gujarat Titans.

The 33-year-old brings considerable experience, having won five IPL titles during his career, including four with Mumbai and one as Gujarat captain.

His ability to contribute with both bat and ball gives Punjab another high-profile option as they prepare for the 2027 season.

However, the trade also means Punjab must rebuild part of their bowling attack following Arshdeep's departure.

Replacing a bowler who has led the franchise's wicket-taking charts will be a major challenge.

## Mumbai Indians Enter a New Era

Hardik's exit comes during a broader transformation at Mumbai Indians.

The franchise has also made significant changes to its coaching setup, with former West Indies allrounder Kieron Pollard taking over as head coach from Mahela Jayawardene.

Robin Uthappa has been appointed batting coach, Mitchell McClenaghan will oversee the bowling department, and T Dilip has joined as fielding coach.

With a new coaching team, a vacant captaincy position and Arshdeep joining Bumrah in the pace attack, Mumbai Indians are preparing for a different look in IPL 2027.

For Punjab Kings, the arrival of Hardik could prove equally significant.

The trade gives both teams a chance to reset, but how successfully they adjust to these changes will become clear when the new IPL season begins.

title: Saqib Khan Takes Seven on Test Debut as Pakistan Fight Back Against Sri Lanka
author: Azmat Nawaz
tags: Pakistan Cricket, Rawalpindi Test, Pakistan vs Sri Lanka, Kusal Mendis, PAK vs SL, Saqib Khan, Test Cricket
summary: Saqib Khan claims seven wickets on Test debut as Pakistan fight back against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi, but rain threatens to force a draw.
body:
![](/images/news/wp/Triumphant-Pakistani-Cricketer-Celebration.jpg)

**RAWALPINDI:** A dream debut for Saqib Khan turned Pakistan's fortunes around in Rawalpindi on Thursday, as the young fast bowler ripped through Sri Lanka's batting lineup with seven wickets to bring the hosts back into the opening Test.

Sri Lanka began the day firmly in control at 404-4, but Saqib had other ideas. His outstanding spell sparked a stunning collapse, with the visitors losing their final six wickets for just 42 runs to finish on 446.

The debutant returned figures of 7-130, giving Pakistan a much-needed lift after Sri Lanka had dominated the previous day's play.

### Saqib Khan Sparks Dramatic Sri Lankan Collapse

Saqib wasted little time making his presence felt. In the opening over, he removed Dhananjaya de Silva, who had resumed on an unbeaten 167.

De Silva failed to add to his overnight score, edging a delivery into the gloves of wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori.

The breakthrough gave Pakistan fresh energy, and Saqib continued to pile pressure on the Sri Lankan batters.

Captain Kusal Mendis also fell to the debutant, dealing another major blow to the visitors.

Saqib went on to dismiss Sonal Dinusha for 20 before cleaning up the tail with the wickets of Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando.

What had looked like a potentially massive Sri Lankan total was suddenly restricted to 446, leaving Pakistan trailing by just 12 runs on the first innings.

### Seven Wickets and a Place in Pakistan's Record Books

Saqib's performance was more than just a match-changing spell. It also earned him a place among some of Pakistan's most memorable Test debutants.

He became only the fourth Pakistani bowler to take seven wickets in an innings on Test debut, joining Mohammad Zahid, Mohammad Nazir and Abrar Ahmed.

Zahid achieved figures of 7-66, Nazir claimed 7-99, while Abrar recorded 7-114 on his debut.

For Saqib, it was the kind of introduction to international cricket that few players could have imagined.

### Pakistan Build a Lead Before Weather Intervenes

Pakistan's second innings began with an early setback when Tayyab Arif was trapped lbw by Asitha Fernando for 11 shortly before lunch.

But Azan Awais and Mohammad Taha steadied the innings, putting together an unbeaten partnership to keep Pakistan in control.

Awais reached 22 not out, while Taha remained unbeaten on 24 as Pakistan moved to 57-1.

Just as the hosts were beginning to build momentum, rain and deteriorating light brought proceedings to a premature close.

Pakistan ended the day with a lead of 45 runs and nine wickets remaining.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-12-2026-12_43_42-PM-1024x683.jpg)

### Rain Could Decide the Fate of Rawalpindi Test

Despite Pakistan's impressive comeback, the weather may have the final say.

With more rain forecast for Friday and valuable playing time already lost, the possibility of a draw is growing.

That would leave both teams heading into the second and final Test with everything still to play for.

The series finale is scheduled to begin in Rawalpindi on November 17.

For now, however, the spotlight belongs to Saqib Khan, whose remarkable seven-wicket debut has given Pakistan something to celebrate in an otherwise rain-hit contest.

summary: ICC proposes tougher T20 league regulations, including overseas player limits and anti-corruption rules that could impact ILT20 and MLC.
body:
![](/images/news/wp/ILT20-Purple-Trophy-Press-Stage.jpg)

The rapid growth of franchise cricket could be heading for a major shake-up, with the International Cricket Council (ICC) considering tighter regulations that could change how T20 leagues operate around the world.

At the heart of the proposals is a push to give the ICC greater authority over franchise competitions, including stricter limits on overseas players, stronger anti-corruption measures and tougher scrutiny of league finances.

The proposed changes could have particularly serious consequences for the UAE's International League T20 (ILT20) and Major League Cricket (MLC) in the United States, both of which have built much of their appeal around international stars.

The recommendations, prepared by an ICC review group, are expected to be discussed during the governing body's meetings in Bali this weekend.

### Overseas Player Restrictions Could Hit ILT20 and MLC

One of the most significant proposals concerns the number of overseas players allowed in a team's starting XI.

Under the proposed approach, franchise teams would be limited to four overseas players, potentially forcing some leagues to make major changes to their squads.

The ILT20 currently permits up to nine overseas players in its playing XI, including at least one from an Associate Member nation.

MLC, meanwhile, allows teams to field as many as six overseas players.

Both competitions previously received exemptions from overseas-player restrictions introduced in 2023.

Removing those exemptions could create immediate challenges for franchises that depend on established international cricketers to attract viewers, sponsors and commercial investment.

Teams would need to rely much more heavily on domestic talent, particularly players from the UAE and United States.

While that could create additional opportunities for emerging local cricketers, it could also affect the competitive strength and commercial appeal of both competitions.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-12-2026-02_57_08-PM.webp)

### ICC Wants More Authority Over Franchise Competitions

The proposals go well beyond overseas-player limits.

At present, cricket boards representing Full Member nations have considerable freedom to approve franchise leagues within their territories.

For example, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is responsible for sanctioning the Indian Premier League.

Under the proposed framework, the ICC would gain the power to review those approvals and intervene if a national board failed to meet the required standards.

In serious cases, the governing body could reject an application or withdraw an existing league's approval.

Such a change would represent a significant shift in how franchise cricket is regulated internationally.

### Corruption Concerns Drive Push for Stronger Oversight

The growing number of domestic T20 competitions has also raised concerns about corruption, unreliable ownership and delayed player payments.

The ICC review group believes more thorough checks are needed before leagues receive permission to operate.

Organisers could be required to demonstrate that they have reliable financial backing, appropriate player-payment protections and effective anti-corruption systems.

Another proposal would require competitions to use either the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit or an integrity team approved by the governing body.

Leagues considered particularly vulnerable to corruption could face additional scrutiny.

If officials determine that the risks cannot be adequately controlled, a competition could be denied approval.

The recommendations reflect growing concern about the challenges of maintaining integrity as franchise cricket expands into new markets.

### Betting Sponsorships Could Face Restrictions

Commercial partnerships are another major focus of the proposed reforms.

The review group wants to restrict sponsorship arrangements involving betting companies or businesses that indirectly promote gambling in markets where it is prohibited.

The proposed restrictions could affect competitions such as South Africa's SA20, where betting-related sponsorship has become part of the commercial landscape.

The ICC's concern is that such arrangements may expose cricket to illegal gambling activity and increase the risk of corruption.

League organisers could therefore face additional pressure to reconsider certain sponsorship agreements.

### New Approval Fees and Player Payments Under Discussion

The review group has also recommended introducing a fee for leagues seeking official approval.

The money could help cover background checks, financial investigations and anti-corruption work.

Another issue under consideration is the standardisation of solidarity payments.

These payments are made to cricket boards whose players participate in overseas franchise competitions, recognising the boards' role in developing international talent.

Currently, payment arrangements can vary between cricket authorities, sometimes creating disagreements over player participation.

A more consistent system could simplify negotiations and reduce disputes between leagues and national boards.

### Legends Leagues and Growing T20 Calendar Also Under Review

The ICC is also examining the rise of competitions involving former international players.

Legends leagues have become increasingly popular, but the review group believes they raise questions about player eligibility and anti-corruption oversight.

Officials are expected to consider whether these tournaments should fall under the same regulatory framework as other franchise competitions.

There is also discussion about potentially limiting the number of leagues that a cricket board can sanction within its territory.

Such restrictions could help protect the international calendar, which has come under increasing pressure from the expansion of franchise cricket.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-12-2026-02_57_13-PM-1.webp)

### What Happens Next?

The proposals have been prepared by a review group chaired by former Bangladesh opener and current Bangladesh Cricket Board president Tamim Iqbal.

The group also includes senior officials from the England and Wales Cricket Board, Cricket Australia and the BCCI.

The recommendations will be considered by the ICC's Chief Executives' Committee, with proposals requiring formal approval potentially moving to the ICC board.

For now, no final decision has been announced.

But if the reforms are adopted, they could reshape the business of T20 cricket, forcing leagues to reconsider how they recruit players, attract sponsors and operate.

For competitions such as ILT20 and MLC, the outcome could be particularly important as they seek to establish themselves in an increasingly crowded global cricket market.

title: Saud Shakeel's 97 Helps Pakistan Secure Draw Against Sri Lankain Rawalpindi Test
author: Azmat Nawaz
tags: Rawalpindi Test, Saud Shakeel, Pakistan vs Sri Lanka, Babar Azam, PAK vs SL, Saqib Khan
summary: Saud Shakeel scores a fighting 97 as Pakistan draw the first Test against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi despite a tense final-day collapse.
body:
![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-13-2026-09_49_28-AM-1024x820.jpg)

**RAWALPINDI**: Saud Shakeel fell agonisingly short of a century for the second time in the match, but his determined 97 helped Pakistan escape with a draw against Sri Lanka in the first Test at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday.

Pakistan were under serious pressure on the final day after losing five wickets before lunch. Sri Lanka sensed an opportunity to force a result, but Shakeel refused to give in, holding the innings together as Pakistan reached 284-8 before the teams agreed to end the match.

The left-hander had already scored 93 in the first innings and once again showed his ability to handle pressure. His second-innings knock lasted 210 balls and included seven boundaries before Lahiru Kumara finally ended his resistance.

### Shakeel and Ghori frustrate Sri Lanka

Pakistan's position looked increasingly difficult when they slipped to 125-5, with Sri Lanka's bowlers making early inroads.

Shakeel found a reliable partner in Ghazi Ghori, who contributed a valuable 35. Together, they added 92 runs for the sixth wicket, gradually taking the game away from Sri Lanka.

The partnership proved crucial. While Shakeel kept the scoreboard moving, Ghori provided the support Pakistan needed to survive a difficult final day.

Sri Lanka continued to push for wickets, but the visitors could not break through quickly enough to put themselves in a position to win.

Milan Rathnayaka finished as Sri Lanka's most successful bowler with figures of 3-47. Asitha Fernando and Lahiru Kumara picked up two wickets apiece.

### Early wickets put Pakistan under pressure

Sri Lanka began the final morning with renewed energy, and it took just one delivery for Kumara to make an impact.

He removed overnight batter Azan Awais for 22 with the first ball of the day. Fernando followed in the next over, dismissing Mohammad Taha for 24 as Pakistan slipped to 57-3.

Captain Babar Azam joined Shakeel and briefly steadied the innings. The pair added 50 runs for the fourth wicket before Rathnayaka dismissed Babar for 34, with the Pakistan captain falling into a carefully placed leg-side field.

Salman Agha also struggled to settle and departed for 13, leaving Pakistan in trouble at 125-5.

By lunch, Pakistan were 151-5, holding a lead of only 139 runs. Sri Lanka still had hopes of forcing a victory, but Shakeel's resistance eventually shut the door.

### Saqib Khan's seven wickets keep Pakistan in the contest

The match had already witnessed several dramatic shifts in momentum.

Pakistan declared their first innings at 434-9, but Sri Lanka responded strongly through centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis.

The visitors appeared set for a substantial first-innings advantage before Pakistan debutant Saqib Khan produced an outstanding spell.

Sri Lanka lost their final four wickets for just 42 runs, slipping from 404-6 to 446 all out.

Saqib finished with impressive figures of 7-130, giving Pakistan a way back into the contest after Sri Lanka's middle-order dominance.

### Weather denies both teams a decisive result

Rain interruptions and fading light repeatedly disrupted play throughout the five days.

A total of 117 overs were lost to poor weather and light, leaving both teams with limited time to push for victory.

Pakistan captain Babar Azam acknowledged the efforts of Sri Lanka's batters while praising Saqib's contribution with the ball.

"We should also give credit to Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis for the way they built the partnership before Saqib bowled superbly," Babar said.

Kusal Mendis, meanwhile, felt Sri Lanka had missed an opportunity to take control earlier in the match.

"We won a good toss but did not do well in the first session, and that's where we need to learn. But overall I am happy," he said.

![](/images/news/wp/ChatGPT-Image-Nov-12-2026-12_43_42-PM-1-1024x683.jpg)

### Pakistan and Sri Lanka turn attention to second Test

The draw leaves the two-match series level at 0-0.

For Pakistan, Shakeel's twin innings of 93 and 97 were among the biggest positives, while Saqib's seven-wicket haul offered encouragement for the bowling attack.

Sri Lanka will take confidence from their strong batting performance but may reflect on the opportunities they failed to convert.

Both teams will meet again at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday, November 17, for the second and final Test, with the series still up for grabs.
seoTitle: Saud Shakeel's 97 Helps Pakistan Draw Sri Lanka Test
